assertions.description: During the Chrome 151 origin trial the shipping surface is navigator.rtc (Chromium rtc.idl); with the RTCDiagnosticLogging feature enabled on a secure context, navigator.rtc is an object.
navigator.rtc.startDiagnosticLogging is a function that begins a capture and resolves with a session UUID string.
navigator.rtc.finishDiagnosticLogging is a function that finalises the locally stored log.
navigator.rtc.cancelDiagnosticLogging is a function that discards captured data.
The interface is [SecureContext]: on a non-secure context navigator.rtc must be absent (on a secure context either state is legal because the runtime feature also gates exposure).

When the surface is bound, startDiagnosticLogging() resolves with a non-empty string session ID (the spec promises a UUID; the log itself is never exposed to the page). Cleans up with cancelDiagnosticLogging().
assertions.test: (async()=>{ if (typeof navigator.rtc?.startDiagnosticLogging !== 'function') return false; const id = await navigator.rtc.startDiagnosticLogging(); try { await navigator.rtc.cancelDiagnosticLogging(); } catch (_) {} return typeof id === 'string' && id.length > 0; })()

assertions.description: When bound, startDiagnosticLogging() with 6 metadata entries rejects before recording (draft spec says TypeError, Chromium rtc.cc rejects RangeError 'Too many metadata entries.' — either error name proves enforcement).
assertions.test: (async()=>{ if (typeof navigator.rtc?.startDiagnosticLogging !== 'function') return false; const m = {}; for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) m['k' + i] = 'v'; try { await navigator.rtc.startDiagnosticLogging({ metadata: m }); return false; } catch (e) { return !!e && (e.name === 'TypeError' || e.name === 'RangeError'); } })()

assertions.description: Divergence watch: the current WICG draft puts the methods as statics on RTCPeerConnection. This assertion records whether this browser has caught up with the draft (it is EXPECTED to fail on Chrome 151's navigator.rtc trial surface — a fail here documents the divergence, not a broken page).
